name: François Jacob
summary: French biologist and Nobel laureate known for discoveries concerning genetic control of enzyme and virus synthesis.

name: Simon Jacob
summary: Father of François Jacob, combined religious practice with radical-socialist opinions.

name: Thérèse Franck
summary: Mother of François Jacob, agnostic and politically conservative.

name: Albert Franck
summary: Maternal grandfather of François Jacob, first Jew to reach the rank of lieutenant general.

name: André Lwoff
summary: French microbiologist and head of the laboratory where François Jacob worked at Institut Pasteur.

name: Jacques Monod
summary: French biologist and collaborator of François Jacob on the operon model.

name: Elie Wollman
summary: French biologist who collaborated with François Jacob on bacterial conjugation.

name: Arthur Pardee
summary: US researcher who participated in the PaJaMo experiment.

name: Sydney Brenner
summary: Biologist who collaborated with François Jacob on messenger RNA discovery.

name: Francis Crick
summary: Biologist who concluded substance X was RNA during a meeting with Jacob and Brenner.

name: Christine Petit
summary: Author of the tribute article, specialist in Genetics and Cellular Physiology.

name: Philippe Sansonetti
summary: Author of the tribute article, specialist in Microbiology and Infectious Diseases.

name: Institut Pasteur
summary: French biology research centre where François Jacob conducted much of his work.

name: Collège de France
summary: French research and higher education institution where Jacob held the Chair of Cell Genetics.

name: Free France
summary: Government in exile and military force led by Charles de Gaulle during WWII.

name: Senegalese infantry regiment
summary: Military unit where François Jacob was appointed during WWII.

name: Cabanel centre
summary: Army-created centre to produce antibiotics where Jacob wrote his medical thesis.

name: Académie française
summary: French council of authorities on matters pertaining to the French language, of which Jacob was a member.

name: Paris
summary: Capital city of France where Jacob grew up and fled from in 1940.

name: England
summary: Country where Jacob fled to join Free France in 1940.

name: Dakar
summary: City in Senegal where Jacob was sent in 1940.

name: Normandy
summary: Region in France where Jacob landed on 1 August 1944.

name: Val de Grâce hospital
summary: Hospital in Paris where Jacob was hospitalized after war injuries.

name: Nice
summary: City in France near which Jacob had a house in Mouans-Sarthoux.

name: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
summary: Prestigious award awarded to Jacob, Lwoff, and Monod in 1965.

name: Chair of Cell Genetics
summary: Professorial chair held by François Jacob at Collège de France.

name: La Logique du vivant: une histoire de l'hérédité
summary: Book by François Jacob published in 1970 on the history of heredity.

name: Le Jeu des possibles: essai sur la diversité du vivant
summary: Book by François Jacob published in 1981 on the diversity of life.

name: La Statue intérieure
summary: Autobiography by François Jacob published in 1987.

name: La Souris, la mouche et l'homme
summary: Book by François Jacob published in 1997.

name: Les bactéries lysogènes et la notion de provirus
summary: Monograph by François Jacob published in 1954 compiling his PhD work.

name: PaJaMo experiment
summary: Famous experiment designed by Jacob, Monod, and Pardee to analyze gene products.

name: messenger RNA
summary: RNA molecule whose existence was demonstrated by Jacob and colleagues in 1960.
